item.title: 1: Daily Halacha: Tu BiShvat: Halachic Ramifications of the Day and the Custom of Eating Fruit
item.description:
Tu BiShvat is above all a halachic date, the new year for trees in three laws: orlah, the tithes and bikkurim, and the first two still apply. The custom of eating fruit on the day is first mentioned by the Magen Avraham about four hundred years ago, and the number fifteen came later. It is a fine custom, since every fruit eaten is a chance to appreciate Hashem, but no one need go hunting for exotic fruit.
Daily Halacha — Tu BiShvat Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 2: Daily Halacha: Why Humans Prefer Fruits to Vegetables
item.description:
Why is Tu BiShvat, the new year for fruit trees, celebrated when the other new years in the Mishnah are not? After his sin Adam was told he would eat the grasses of the field, and wept that he and his donkey would eat from one trough. A vegetable is consumed and gone, while a fruit tree and its seeds keep their potential, and a tree reaching upwards is the image of a person who strives to grow.

item.title: 3: Daily Halacha: The Blessing of Shehiyanu on New Fruits and on Fruit Available All Year Round
item.description:
When is Shehehiyanu said on a new fruit? Originally on seeing it, but since the Rosh the custom is to say it only when eating it, and Sefaradim follow the Kaf HaHayim in saying Bore Peri HaEs first, while the Mishnah Berurah reverses the order. It is said only on a fruit of the new season, not on one available all year round, even if one has not eaten it for a long time.

item.title: 4: Daily Halacha: Etrog Jam and Further Shehiyanu Rules
item.description:
Shehehiyanu needs a fruit that is visibly of the new season, so it is not said on nuts, dried fruit or vegetables, even from a new crop. There is a custom, praised by Rav Ovadia Yosef, for women to eat etrog jam on Tu BiShvat as a segulah for children and an easier birth. No Shehehiyanu is said on it, since the etrog stays on the tree all year, Shehehiyanu was already said on Sukkot, and the fruit in jam is not recognisable.
Daily Halacha — Tu BiShvat Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 5: Daily Halacha: What Is Tu BiShvat About?
item.description:
Is Tu BiShvat really about fruit? A halachic new year with three consequences, two relevant today, beginning with orlah, the fruit of a tree in its first four years, before turning to the custom of eating fruit.
